problem: The answer contradicts the chapter's own definition. Section 2 and Q3 say a notification is sent when Present_Value moves by MORE than COV_Increment. The step from 22.6 °C to 23.1 °C is exactly 0.5 °C, which is equal to, not more than, the increment of 0.5 °C. So 23.1 should not trigger a notification. The answer says it does trigger.
fix: Either keep the readings and answer: only 22.6 °C triggers (0.6 > 0.5); 23.1 °C differs from the last reported 22.6 °C by exactly 0.5 °C, which is not greater than the increment, so no notification. Or change the last reading to 23.2 °C, so it differs by 0.6 °C and does trigger; notifications then at 22.6 °C and 23.2 °C.

problem: The stack is drawn and described as four layers: Application, Network, Data link, PHY. The standard WirelessHART stack has five layers; the transport layer between application and network is missing. The text elsewhere talks about end-to-end delivery and retries, which the transport layer is responsible for, so a student may wonder where that sits.
fix: Add a Transport layer between Application and Network (note: 'end-to-end reliability, retries'), giving five layers, and update the caption and aria text to match.
